name: Firefly Choir
promptTemplate: A summer meadow at night under {{glow_style}} skies, where synchronous fireflies couple with {{coupling}} strength at {{tempo}} rhythm, surrounded by {{grass_sway}} swaying reeds.

ui.title: FIREFLY CHOIR
ui.tagline: Tap in rhythm to synchronize the meadow

blink.hint: Flashes your firefly and tugs neighbors into sync

coupling.hint: How strongly nearby fireflies pull each other into phase

tempo.hint: Base pulsing speed of the swarm

glow_style.hint: Changes the night sky and backdrop palette

grass_sway.hint: Toggles swaying grass silhouettes in the meadow

listing.blurb: Fireflies drift across a nocturnal meadow, flashing to individual rhythms until synchronized taps trigger explosive unison shockwaves across the room.
listing.prompt: A summer meadow at night with a firefly for every person, each blinking at its own rhythm: pressing 'blink' flashes yours and nudges the fireflies nearby toward your timing; when the whole room blinks in unison the meadow erupts in waves of light, and the longest streak in sync is kept. Make it a party game a whole room can follow from across the floor: bold shapes and bright colours on a dark ground, every player drawn in their own hue, big short labels (a score, GO!, the winner) in a heavy font, and a large, satisfying reaction on screen the instant anyone presses. It must work with one player or forty, scaling its lanes, seats or pieces to room.people and coping with people joining and leaving mid-round; play itself in a lively attract mode whenever nobody has pressed anything for a few seconds; and after a winner is shown, start the next round on its own. Keep it lean: game state in bounded arrays in room.state, nothing allocated inside hot loops, a steady 60fps at 1920x1080.
